ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a D flip-flop FF0, on the left side there is a CLK clock input terminal, and a triangle symbol is used to indicate edge triggering; on the right side there is a Q output and a Q-bar complementary output with an overline. The wiring shows that the Q-bar output is fed back and connected to the D input on the left side, while the Q output is brought out as the output terminal. Reasoning: For a rising-edge-triggered D flip-flop, after each clock rising edge there is Q_next = D. Since in the figure D = Q-bar, every time a clock rising edge comes, Q will become the opposite state of the original, that is, the flip-flop toggles once for each clock pulse. Q needs two clock cycles to complete one full period, therefore the output frequency is half of the input clock frequency. The input clock frequency is 10 kHz, so f_Q = 10/2 = 5 kHz.

method.method_draft: First read the circuit image: the D input is connected to the complement output Q-bar, not to Q, so the flip-flop is configured as a toggle/divide-by-2 circuit. Then read the text: the applied clock frequency is 10 kHz and the output frequency is requested at Q. Apply Q_next = D at every rising edge; with D = Q-bar, Q changes state on every clock edge. One full period of Q therefore takes two clock periods, so f_Q = 10/2 = 5 kHz.
